skill.name: writing-hookify-rules
skill.description: Guides users through creating Hookify rule files that warn or block commands, file edits, prompts, and completion checks.
skill.summary: Create local Hookify rules for Claude Code guardrails using YAML frontmatter and regex patterns.
skill.author: anthropics

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent guardrails for AI coding sessions. This skill helps create Hookify rules that warn or block risky commands, edits, prompts, and stop events.
actual_capabilities: Explains the Hookify rule file format with YAML frontmatter and a markdown message body.
Shows how to create simple single-pattern rules and multi-condition rules.
Covers bash, file, stop, prompt, and all-event rule types.
Provides regex examples for command safety, file edits, sensitive files, and workflow checks.
Describes local file naming, project placement, testing, refining, disabling, and deleting rules.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not install, run, or validate Hookify itself.
Generated patterns still need project-specific testing before teams rely on them.
Regex examples may miss edge cases or match harmless text in some projects.
Rules can only use Hookify events, fields, and operators supported by the host plugin.

use_cases.title: Block risky shell commands
use_cases.description: Create warning or blocking rules for destructive commands, broad permission changes, or privileged operations.

use_cases.title: Warn on sensitive file edits
use_cases.description: Guide agents when edits touch environment files, credential names, certificate files, or generated output.

use_cases.title: Enforce team completion checks
use_cases.description: Add stop-event reminders for tests, builds, documentation, reviews, or deployment readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple warning rule
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner rule for one risky command pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hookify rule that warns before an agent uses a recursive delete command. Include the event, pattern, message, and test advice.

prompt_templates.title: Add a file edit guardrail
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate rule for matching a file path and new text.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Hookify rule that warns when an edit adds an API key pattern to an environment file. Explain each condition.

prompt_templates.title: Design a stop checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Workflow rule that runs when the agent wants to finish.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a stop-event Hookify rule that reminds the agent to run tests, check the build, and update documentation before stopping.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a rule set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of existing rule ideas for coverage and false positives.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Hookify rule goals and propose better names, events, operators, patterns, and messages. Explain likely false positives and test cases.

output_examples.input: Create a rule that warns before deleting files recursively.
output_examples.output: A focused bash-event rule proposal with a descriptive name, a recursive delete pattern, a warning message, and a short testing checklist.

output_examples.input: Warn when a TypeScript edit adds console logging.
output_examples.output: A multi-condition file-event rule plan that matches TypeScript paths, detects console logging in new text, and suggests safer logging practices.

output_examples.input: Add a completion reminder for deployment work.
output_examples.output: A stop-event checklist rule that asks the agent to confirm tests, review, monitoring, and deployment readiness before ending the session.

best_practices: Use narrow patterns that match the risky behavior, then test them against safe and unsafe examples.
Write messages that explain the risk and provide a clear next action.
Store local rules with descriptive names and keep project-specific rules out of shared commits when needed.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on broad patterns that match common words in unrelated code or prompts.
Do not use blocking actions before the team has tested false positives in real workflows.
Do not create silent warnings that describe a problem without a practical alternative.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps write Hookify rules that warn or block AI agent actions based on events, fields, operators, and patterns.

faq.question: Does the skill execute shell commands?
faq.answer: No. It documents rule patterns and examples. Users must test any generated rule in their own project.

faq.question: Can it create blocking rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to use warn or block actions and how each action affects supported events.

faq.question: Can it inspect my repository automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can help design rules from details you provide, but repository inspection depends on the host assistant tools.

faq.question: How should I test a rule?
faq.answer: Try examples that should match and examples that should not match. Refine the pattern until false positives are acceptable.

faq.question: Are local rule files meant for version control?
faq.answer: The skill recommends local Hookify rule filenames and notes that local rule files can be excluded from commits.
